outline: 本課程精選有關教育與文化之文章，引導學生從閱讀中印證，比較各種文化和教育現象，並鼓勵學生從各種不同角度蒐集資料，俾使課堂討論呈現時代性與多元化的觀點。
schedule:
09/16	Introduction
09/23	Michael K's birth, childhood, disposition, and occupation; Anna K and her
illness; the settings of the novel (pp. 3-16)
09/30	The Ks' application and wait for travel permits (pp. 16-28)
Oral Presentation 1:
10/07	The death of Anna K in a hospital in Stellenbosch; Michael K robbed by a
soldier (pp. 28-41)
Oral Presentation 2:
10/14	Michael K forced to labor; walking to Prince Albert; living on charity; arriving
at Prince Albert; and hunting goats (pp. 41-54)
Oral Presentation 3:
10/21	Michael K learning a lesson, burying his mother's ashes, and beginning his
life as a cultivator; the unexpected visit of a deserter from the army; the Visagie
grandson's assignment; Michael K running away (pp. 54-67)
Oral Presentation 4:
10/28	Michael K's life in the mountains and in the Jakkalsdrif labor camp (pp. 67-80)
Oral Presentation 5:
11/04	The function of the camp; Michael K's negotiation with a guard; Michael K
forced to labor; the condition for leaving the Jakkalsdrif camp (pp. 80-93)
11/11	Oosthuizen's wrath; Robert's influence; Michael K shouting for help; Michael
K's escape from the camp and return to the Visagie farm; Michael K's life on the farm
(pp. 93-106)
11/18	Michael K's confidence, fear, and anxiety; his hiding in a cave; his freedom; the
idea of the parasite; his dreams; his appetite (pp. 106-119)
Oral Presentation 6:
11/25	Michael K discovered by the soldiers; Captain Oosthuizen's recognition of
Michael K; heavy explosions—end of Part One—Michael K's detention at the
Kenilworth camp (pp. 119-132)
Oral Presentation 7:
12/02	The medical officer's narration about Michael K; Noël and the medical officer's
investigation of Michael K (pp. 132-145)
Oral Presentation 8:
12/09	Michael K's refusal to eat; the medical officer's undelivered letter to Michael K;
Michael K's escape from the Kenilworth rehabilitation camp (pp. 145-159)
Oral Presentation 9:
12/16	More prisoners sent to the Kenilworth camp; the medical officer's desire to
follow Michael K; the medical officer's exploration of the significance of Michael K's
refusal to eat; the medical officer's comment on Michael K (pp. 159-167)
General Discussion on The Childhood of Jesus: All
12/23	Michael K's return to Sea Point, Cape Town; his harassment by a pimp and two
prostitutes; his pursuit of an independent living as a gardener (pp. 169-184)
12/30	Review
01/06	Final Exam
01/13	Discussion
assessment: attendance: 20%; quiz and presentation: 30%; final exam: 50%
